## 5. The physical-model consequence—and the global test it must pass

Consider a regular cellulation of a three-dimensional ball, with one binary control on every edge and signed plaquette energy

\[
E(x)
=
-\sum_pJ_p(-1)^{(\partial_2^{\mathsf T}x)_p}.
\]

Here \(\partial_2\) maps faces to their edge boundaries. All edge controls, including boundary edges, remain free.

Construct the dual graph with one vertex per three-cell plus an exterior vertex, and one dual edge per face. Its incidence matrix \(B\) has the same row space as \(\partial_3^{\mathsf T}\).

The ball’s second homology vanishes:

\[
\ker\partial_2=\operatorname{im}\partial_3.
\]

Consequently,

\[
\ker B
=
(\operatorname{im}\partial_3)^\perp
=
(\ker\partial_2)^\perp
=
\operatorname{im}\partial_2^{\mathsf T}.
\]

This is exactly the required global code equality.

An unknown invertible binary recoding of the controls preserves every dependency among the frequency masks. The algorithm can therefore acquire and minimize the energy even when its visible interactions have become dense and high order. It need not recover the original lattice or recoding.

Matching-based ground-state methods for supplied random-plaquette gauge models already exist. The completed operation here starts earlier, at scalar observations, and acquires a sufficient global representation before applying that machinery. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="6"}

### Periodic boundaries expose the lost joint information

On a three-torus, the local cube equations omit three global flux constraints.

For the executed periodic \(3\times3\times3\) instance:

\[
m=81,\qquad
\operatorname{rank}A=52,\qquad
\operatorname{rank}B_{\mathrm{local}}=26.
\]

Although

\[
B_{\mathrm{local}}A=0,
\]

the local cycle space has dimension \(81-26=55\), while the attainable space has dimension \(52\). The three-dimensional gap is real.

The program’s full graph-recognition step rejected that support from the proved class. It did not silently optimize over the larger space allowed by the local equations. This rejection is scoped to the construction; it establishes no hardness result for periodic gauge minimization. The matrices and checks are reproduced in the :chatgpt-content-reference{index="10"}[experiment record](sandbox:/workspace/scratch/7c78cedfa162/p3_design/results.json).

8. The capability’s exact boundary

The mechanism succeeds because the acquired joint sign space has a particular tractable geometry. Several nearby changes break the argument.

Reversing the duality changes the optimization problem. A graphic frequency matroid produces a cut-space problem, and arbitrary signed optimization then contains Max-Cut. General regularity is insufficient.

The promise cannot be certified from unrestricted black-box observations. A function can agree with every queried point yet contain an unobserved spike that changes its optimum. The graph certificate proves a complete fact about the acquired representation. It does not certify that an arbitrary physical system has no additional dense-spectrum effect. The cographic promise supplies the sparsity bound, but the promise itself remains a model assumption.
